title: (No AI) Researchers are getting tired of OpenAI gatekeeping its breakthroughs
author: Robert Hart
content:
![Frowning calculator on a background of math writing.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/STKS537_AI_MATH_7.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

On Monday, OpenAI [announced](https://openai.com/index/building-scientific-understanding-with-academic-communities/) impressive [breakthroughs](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1019143/openai-eth-kaseya-science-math-physics) in mathematics, computer science, and physics, along with what the company says is an evolving approach to communicating its findings. But despite its apparent course correction, researchers who spoke to _The Verge_ are growing increasingly tired of the company's antics.

It has been a turbulent few months between OpenAI and mathematicians, who are still grappling with the hundreds of preprints [unceremoniously dumped on them](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1008726/openai-mathematics-solutions-chaos) at the start of October. This time, OpenAI says it is working with expert "shepherds" to decide how best to share its latest breakthroughs.

title: (No AI) VisionQuest is what happens when AI really goes rogue
author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
content:
![Four characters from VisionQuest are seated on a couch in a living room.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/107-90190_RC.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

In Marvel's _VisionQuest_, a superpowered robot tries to better understand humanity by getting lost in elaborate, digital daydreams in which he and other artificial intelligence-powered beings live together in a home. The series is deeply fantastical, yet it plays with some of the ideas that have come to dominate the conversation about real-world generative artificial intelligence, exploring whether we should look at thinking machines as people and if AI truly poses the kind of existential danger that should keep us up at night. It's also a reminder how aggressively Silicon Valley has used the trappings of science fiction to sell us on its AI …
